Summary: Enterprise evaluation focused on Private VPC deployment and audit logging parity. Primary ask: SIEM export and canonical log schema that meets financial-services audit standards (7+ year retention for key records).

Recent timeline:
- 2026-02-18: Intro security review (AE + SE + Ironclad security team). Fireflies ff_2026-02-18_8234. High-level ask: turnkey export to Splunk and S3 with region restrictions.
- 2026-02-25: Tech deep-dive with Miles — discussed log schemas, sampling, and retention tiers. Recorded: ff_2026-02-25_?.
- 2026-03-02: Demo of Private control plane and audit log UI. Follow-up items recorded in thread-CAJkX-kms-questions-20260301.
- 2026-03-05: Security questionnaire submitted (shared drive doc). Jira RRD-4123 opened for KMS integration question set.

Audit logging requirements (customer stated):
- SIEM export options: Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC), syslog forwarder, Kafka topic, or S3 object delivery for bulk archives. Must support TLS+mutual auth.
- Canonical log schema: customer requires fields: timestamp, tenant_id, request_id, api_key_id (masked), user_id (if present), model_id, model_variant, prompt_hash, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, node_id, container_id, kv_cache_hit (bool), routing_decision, fallback_reason, response_error_code, storage_s3_path (if cached), encryption_context (KMS key ARN), and event_type (request|response|admin_action|policy_change).
- Access logs: record all console and API admin actions (who, what, when, where, ip, session_id). Immutable admin audit trail for rollouts/fallbacks.
- Retention & tiering: immediate searchable index in customer SIEM for 90-180 days; archived raw events to customer-owned S3 in eu-west-1 (customer requirement) with 7-year retention on select event types (policy_change, admin_action, billing-relevant, legal_hold). Need lifecycle policy guidance.
- Tamper evidence & integrity: support for HMAC signing of batches or WORM storage on archive bucket; log export must include checksum and manifest for ingestion.

KMS integration specifics requested:
- Customer uses AWS KMS with customer-managed CMKs and requires envelope encryption: Redwood must accept customer public key context or use provided CMK by ARN when writing archives.
- KMS usage logging: ensure CloudTrail events show Redwood access to CMK; map to audit trail entries.
- Key rotation & access model: allow rotation without losing ability to decrypt archived logs (suggest envelope keys + metadata stored in archive manifest).

Operational concerns raised:
- Log cardinality and cost — customer wants guidance on sampling vs full telemetry. Proposed: full audit-level events always retained; sampling for verbose debug traces (configurable).
- Schema evolution: need backwards-compatible fields and a version field in every event.
- Onboarding PoC: send 48 hours of sample traffic (anonymized) to customer's Splunk dev index; validate field extractions, dashboards, and retention lifecycle.

POC & next milestones:
- Deliver canonical SIEM log schema (this artifact) + 10 sample events (actionable) by 2026-03-12.
- Setup Splunk HEC ingest in dev account and send test events (AE + SE pairing) by 2026-03-18.
- KMS integration dry-run with RRD-4199: confirm CMK policy and test envelope encryption by 2026-03-24.
- Legal to review updated contract clause for log residency and retention (blocker).

Stated quotes / paraphrase from security lead:
- "We need an auditable, tamper-evident trail that can live in our EU account for the long term — anything else is a non-starter."
